Environment: the driver's removal list, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1, both selection variables, and an exact frozen environment; the provider's _check_python mirrored exactly. T-05 right. Blocked in place (TR-01).
answers.Q4: One start per row through the real Darwin run_process compiled from verified bytes; keeps stdout, stderr, exit, receipt and started record; counts by P07 section 4. Predicates insufficient (TR-02, TR-03, TR-10). T-03 right. It can start Node for a row whose fixtures differ (TR-03).
answers.Q5: Independent (standard library only) and faithful to the probe's lines 749-821 and the test's 119-161: inventory of 2,060 rows, differences, thresholds (5e-6 for [0..2][3], positions and bounds; 1e-6 otherwise), decisions, completeness, no duplicates, order; Q01/Q03 pass every row; the negative has exactly one failed row and finding at left/base matrix_0_3. T-10's 1e-9 bound is sound for these fixtures. Retained bounds and vertices not recomputed (TR-15).
answers.Q6: Covers child_process, worker_threads, cluster, Worker, dlopen, process.binding (raw only), _linkedBinding, internalBinding, execve, computed require/import, createRequire, Module._load, module.constructor and process.mainModule (dot forms), vm, eval and Function; misses binding names, bracket forms, receiver-qualified and parenthesized calls (TR-11); wasi is not a process route. Real files: none_found, equal to W2's scan; one missed call shape in the validator preamble. Links and inventory handling sound. The module loader is correctly tools/three_loader.mjs, one of the 24.
answers.Q7: T-01 acceptable as a stated, labelled substitution; T-02's claim right with a nuance; the recorder cannot let a real start through; host-state and T-08 right.
answers.Q8: Complete for refused, failed and unknown outcomes; no retry; absence by ESRCH only, never by name; presence handling unsafe (TR-05); probe code not fixed (TR-16).
answers.Q9: Node only from frozen rows and the cohort's provider; Git only as the provider's HOST-bound reads (T-07); no ldd or codesign. Writes only outputs and by-design evidence; -B enforced except in three entry points (TR-17). One public file leaks private strings (TR-04). discover and mc29 record ambient environments, and the hooks record children's (TR-06).

findings.change: Admit exactly the running tool's own __main__ (realpath equal to its __file__), record it, keep refusing every other preloaded root module; add an in-place test for each tool.
findings.effect: The collector cannot run the cohort as its README launches it (the provider's root must be the worktree); the runner and the current discovery refuse with --root <worktree>. Fail-closed, but S7 would stop; a byte-identical copy outside the worktree would be an unstated path change against P07 section 3.
findings.evidence: discover_inventory.py run from that path inside a verified copy, --root the copy: exit 2, REFUSED, rule PYTHON, modules ['__main__'] (discovery-inplace-w3.json); the collector and runner hold the same check.
findings.issue: Each tool refuses when a module of --root is already loaded; the tool itself is sys.modules['__main__'] and lies under the root once the tooling sits in docs/.../macos-qualification-p35/tooling/ and --root is the worktree.
findings.title: Three tools refuse to run from their committed place against the worktree

findings.change: Add the expected supervisor error to each row (exactly 'Child exited with status N' with code OTRAY-E-BACKEND and state REJECTED for N != 0; null for 0), require equality for the raised Stop and the receipt's error; test with a descendant-leaving stand-in and a staged link.
findings.effect: A row that exits with the expected status and text is COMPLETED and met although the supervisor refused it: a failed run shown as a pass.
findings.issue: expectation_met checks exit status, substrings and paths but not supervisor_failure or the receipt's error. After the child exits, the supervisor can raise a remaining-descendant Stop, an inventory Stop (link, non-private file, byte ceilings, 2,048 entries), a deadline Stop, a log-ceiling Stop or a converted KeyboardInterrupt, each with the child's real returncode and usually a passed cleanup.
findings.title: The direct-probe runner ignores the supervisor's own refusal

findings.change: Require every file_includes and present_paths target absent at intent; add each row's frozen input descriptors and the stage's exact entry set, verified immediately before the start; change the test.
findings.effect: A failed or unfrozen run can be recorded as met; a Node start can be made on unfrozen fixtures.
findings.issue: A file_includes or present_paths target that exists before the start satisfies the predicate. With a stale probe.json in MC36's stage, the probe refuses at approvedEnvelope ('output freshness') on stderr with exit 1, and the stale file meets MC36's predicate; W2's test asserts a row met from a pre-existing probe.json. The rows schema has no input descriptors (P07 section 3 item 7), so Node can start on unfrozen job, configuration, manifest, HOST-copy, GLB or reference bytes.
findings.title: File predicates are not tied to the start, and a row's fixtures are not bound

findings.change: Signal only after identity is established (proc_pidinfo PROC_PIDTBSDINFO start time within the intent-to-started window, proc_pidpath equal to argv[0]); otherwise record 'present, identity not established', send nothing, keep the outcome unknown. findings.issue: Presence is a successful or EPERM probe of a recorded PID or group; after the recorded child exits and is reaped its PID can be reused, and killpg then reaches an unrelated group of the same user. FC-P3's start-time rule names no way to read the kernel's start time, and the records hold no comparable one.
findings.title: FAILURE-CAPTURE FC-P6 signals a recorded group without establishing identity
